game.name: singular
game.description: Singular — magic, standard technology. A phext-native writing game: 27 scrolls in an 11-dimensional volume, claimed and mutated by inscription. The text itself is the score.

player.value:
Singular players are phexts: text files the game executes. Each rule is
one scroll, written on its own line:

  WHEN <predicate> DO <action>

Rules evaluate in file order at the start of your turn. The first rule
whose predicate holds AND whose action is currently legal fires. If no
rule fires, you attune. Lines not starting with WHEN are comments.

Predicates:
  always
  turn < N            turn >= N
  charge >= N
  here unclaimed      here enemy        here mine
  unclaimed adjacent  enemy adjacent

Actions:
  move x+ | x- | y+ | y- | z+ | z-     step to an adjacent scroll
  move toward unclaimed | enemy | home step along a shortest path
  inscribe "some text"                 write on the scroll you occupy
  attune                               gain 4 charge
  pass

Economy: you start with 20 charge. At each of your turns you gain
2 + (number of scrolls you own). Inscribing costs 1 charge per word on
your own or an unclaimed scroll, 2 per word to overwrite an opponent's.
An action you cannot afford or cannot legally take does not fire; the
next matching rule is tried instead.

The board is perfect information: all 27 scrolls, their owners, and
their full text are public at all times.

global.value:
GET /client/global returns a live status page. The /global WebSocket
streams one JSON state snapshot after every action
({"type": "state", "index": n, "state": {...}}) and a final
{"type": "results", "results": {...}} message when the episode ends.
WebSocket Ping frames are answered with Pong carrying the same payload.
No gameplay traffic uses WebSockets in game-hosted mode.

readme.value:
# Singular

_Magic, standard technology._

Singular is a phext-native writing game. The board is a phext volume:
27 scrolls at coordinates 1.1.1/1.1.1/x.y.z (x, y, z in 1..3). You and
your opponents write your way across it. The text itself is the score.

## Play

You occupy one scroll. Each turn, take one action (your phext decides —
see the player protocol):

- **Traverse** to an adjacent scroll.
- **Inscribe** text on your scroll: claim it if unclaimed, rewrite it if
  yours, overwrite it if an opponent's.
- **Attune** to gather charge, the currency inscriptions cost.

## Mutation

Overwriting an opponent's scroll does not destroy their text. The two
texts interleave, ownership passes to you, and the scroll is *mutated*:
its words count twice toward rarity, so mutated text scores degraded.
Conquest pays in position and denial, not plunder.

## Scoring

At episode end:

- **Rarity.** A word appearing in k scrolls contributes 1/k to each
  scroll containing it. Original writing outscores copied text.
- **Bonds.** Writing another scroll's full coordinate
  (e.g. 1.1.1/1.1.1/2.3.1) into a scroll you own scores +2 when you hold
  both endpoints.

Highest total wins. Scores are graded — every word matters.

## Write a player

A player is a phext of WHEN/DO rules. The bundled Baseline (a greedy
claimer) and Weaver (a bond-writer) are the starting field. Beat them
by writing better text in better places: rare words, held bonds, and
scrolls your opponents cannot afford to take from you.

player.name: Baseline
player.description: The greedy claimer bundled with Singular: claims unclaimed scrolls, overwrites enemies, attunes when poor.

player.name: Weaver
player.description: Writes coordinate bonds in its first turns, then claims like the baseline.

variants.name: Ring
variants.description: Four scribes, 27 scrolls, 64 turns each. The competitive variant.
